title: GPU fleet partitioning and tenant isolation: quotas, noisy-neighbor mitigation, and throughput guarantees
creator: Maya Patel
description: Deliver a set of Dedicated GPU fleet controls to partition capacity per tenant, provide hard and soft quota enforcement, and mitigate noisy neighbors while preserving throughput guarantees. This ticket coordinates runtime scheduler changes, an admission/advisor service, console controls, and e2e validation so customers on Dedicated can bind to predictable capacity without risking cross-tenant interference.
background: Customers running on Dedicated have asked for stronger isolation SLAs: guaranteed baseline throughput for committed pools, clear quota enforcement for bursty tenants, and automated detection/mitigation of noisy neighbors that degrade co-tenants. Current behavior uses opportunistic scheduling and per-request fallbacks which can lead to token spikes and tail-latency regressions for sensitive workloads.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce tenant pools: labeled GPU partitions (logical pools) with configurable baseline capacity, burst headroom, and eviction policies. 2) Admission controller that enforces per-tenant active slot quotas and issues burst tokens (short-lived permits) when headroom exists. 3) Scheduler changes to prefer intra-pool packing and respect tenant weights for throughput guarantees. 4) Noisy-neighbor detector that monitors token/latency/kv cache contention and escalates mitigation: transient throttling, eviction to best-effort pool, or automated restart of offending tasks. 5) Console controls to create/update pools and quota policies and dashboarding for isolation metrics.
implementation_plan: Design: schema for tenant pools, quota model (hard vs soft), burst token lifecycle and API
Runtime: scheduler hooks for tenant affinity, slot counting, and burst token checks
Admission service: implement token server with consistent storage, rate limiting, and audit logs
Detector: implement streaming analyzer in metrics pipeline to flag noisy neighbors and calculate per-tenant interference scores
Enforcement: eviction/throttle actions in runtime with safe cooldowns and telemetry
Console & API: CRUD for pools, quota view, and override controls for SRE
Testing: unit tests, integration with dedicated CI, chaos tests for eviction scenarios, and perf benchmarks
Migration: backfill existing Dedicated clusters with default pool mapping and safe cutoff for old scheduling path
acceptance_criteria: Create a tenant pool with baseline 16 vGPU-seconds/sec and burst headroom 4 vGPU-seconds/sec via API; runtime honors baseline under steady load
Hard quota enforcement: when tenant exhausts hard quota, new requests receive 429-like response from admission controller and are recorded in audit logs
Noisy neighbor mitigation: under synthetic contention tests, interfering tenant is detected and throttled within 60s, reducing impact on other tenants by >= 80% in tail-p99 latency
Throughput guarantees: committed tenants maintain >=95% of baseline throughput during co-hosted workloads in 90% of trials
KV cache isolation: per-tenant KV cache namespaces or eviction boundaries proven by integration tests (no cross-tenant key leakage)
Monitoring: dashboards show per-pool active slots, burst token usage, interference score, and alerts trigger on sustained violations
Security review complete and no regressions in role-based controls when changing pool assignments
test_plan: Unit tests for admission token lifecycle, scheduler unit tests for affinity/slot accounting, e2e perf harness that runs mixed tenants (committed, bursty, best-effort) and measures throughput/latency/p99. Chaos tests: simulated GPU OOM and forced long-running tasks to validate eviction logic. Add nightly regressions that compare cost-per-token and tail latency before/after. Include synthetic noisy-neighbor scenarios from datasets in test/fixtures/noisy_neighbor/.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged rollout to internal staging Dedicated clusters. 2) Canary on 2 customer-like clusters with low-risk customers and SRE monitoring. 3) Gradual enablement per-region with opt-in for customers, defaulting to old scheduler for existing contracts for 30 days. 4) After 2 weeks of canary stable metrics, flip default for new Dedicated deployments and provide migration tools. 5) Full enforcement of hard quotas after 90-day notice to existing customers.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add metrics: tenant_active_slots, tenant_baseline_utilization, tenant_burst_tokens_issued, tenant_interference_score, tenant_eviction_actions. Alerts: interference_score > 0.7 for 2m, burst_token_rate > configured threshold for 5m, hard_quota_denials spike > 10/min. Dashboards: per-cluster and per-tenant heatmaps and time-series for troubleshooting.
outstanding_risks: 1) Scheduler complexity may increase median scheduling latency—need microbenchmarks. 2) Admission service single-point-of-failure — design HA and caching. 3) Migration risk: changing default behavior could surface customer workloads that assumed opportunistic capacity. 4) Billing/metric alignment: ensure cost reports reflect reserved vs burst consumption.
notes:
- Prefer admission controller as an independent service to allow cross-cluster policy consistency.
- Consider leveraging existing autoscaler signals (queue depth, average latency) to feed burst token allocation heuristics.
- Work with billing to tag burst vs baseline tokens for invoicing.
- Keep early UI simple: pool create + set baseline/burst/hard-quota; advanced knobs in SRE console only.
